data.argument: The headline rebound is encouraging but not yet durable evidence of a stronger earnings base. Commercial/industrial revenue drove most of the growth, yet related costs and expenses also rose $3.0 million, and management explicitly warns that earnings fluctuate with land-sale timing, leasing activity, and commodity prices. The quarter does not test key thesis supports: TRCC occupancy, Terra Vista leasing, Building 1B delivery, liquidity, and Centennial entitlement progress are all unreported. Lower corporate expenses helped results, but the underlying amount and sustainability are unavailable. Positive peer read-across is mixed: CHCI and FIP grew, while AXR and SRG show how sharply transaction-sensitive this group can be.
key_points: Growth was concentrated in commercial/industrial revenue and may be timing-driven.
Costs rose materially; recurring profitability and expense discipline remain unverified.
Core occupancy, leasing, liquidity, and entitlement catalysts were not tested.
assumptions: No unreported KPI or qualitative update is being inferred.
Commercial/industrial growth includes potentially non-recurring or timing-sensitive activity.
The absence of a reported thesis check is treated as uncertainty, not deterioration.
